title: Calculus
subtitle: Derivatives, integrals, and limits
summary: Differential and integral calculus: limits, derivatives, integrals, and the fundamental theorem.
detail:
Differential calculus studies instantaneous rates of change. The derivative \(f'(x)=\lim_{h\to 0}(f(x+h)-f(x))/h\) measures the slope of \(f\) at \(x\). Key rules: product, quotient, chain. Integral calculus studies accumulation: \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) is the signed area under \(f\).

The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus unites both: if \(F'=f\) then \(\int_a^b f\,dx=F(b)-F(a)\). Techniques include substitution, integration by parts, partial fractions, and trigonometric substitution. Applications span physics, engineering, economics, and every quantitative science.
